question: Why do nurses identify basic human needs when caring for patients?

options.A: To prioritize care effectively for patients
options.B: To eliminate the need for medical diagnosis
options.C: To reduce the hospital stay length strictly
options.D: To replace the standard physician orders

explanation: Spotting basic human needs helps you figure out which urgent care the patient needs right now. You've got this! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: What happens when a person's basic needs are consistently not met?

options.A: Homeostasis is disrupted and illness develops
options.C: Immune system functions at peak efficiency
options.D: Metabolic rate permanently slows down to adapt

explanation: When the body misses out on basics like food, water, or safety, its internal balance gets thrown off, leading to sickness. Every small detail you learn makes you a better nurse! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which level is right at the very bottom of Maslow's hierarchy pyramid?
explanation: Physiological needs (like breathing and eating) form the base because we literally cannot survive without them. Great job reviewing your basics! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why might a nurse sometimes change the strict order of Maslow's hierarchy?

options.A: Individual patient situations can create urgent safety demands
options.B: Psychological needs are always more important than physical ones
options.C: Hospital policies dictate ignoring physiological requirements
options.D: Doctors prefer treating emotional issues before physical ones

explanation: Nursing isn't always one-size-fits-all! If a patient is having an emergency safety crisis, you handle that first. You are learning to think like a real clinician. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: During an emergency resuscitation, which physiological need comes first above all else?
explanation: Air comes first! Without oxygen, nothing else matters. Keep up the brilliant focus! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the main assessment you should do for a patient suffering from severe dehydration?

options.A: Checking understanding of hospital discharge rules
options.B: Evaluating social support systems at home
options.C: Monitoring intake, output, and skin turgor
options.D: Assessing personal self-esteem and body image

explanation: Checking fluids going in and out, plus seeing how skin bounces back, tells you right away how hydrated your patient is. You're doing amazing! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is an important way nurses keep patients physically safe on the ward?

options.A: Preventing falls and checking identification bands
options.B: Providing advanced career counseling for patients
options.C: Promoting high self-esteem through active praise
options.D: Encouraging visits from extended family members

explanation: Simple checks like ID bands and stopping falls protect patients from harm every single day. Excellent clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: How does explaining a medical procedure clearly beforehand help a patient feel secure?

options.A: By replacing the need for informed consent documents
options.B: By reducing fear of the unknown and building trust
options.C: By completely eliminating the risk of surgical complications
options.D: By speeding up the physical wound healing process

explanation: When patients know what to expect, anxiety drops and they trust you more. Communication is a powerful nursing tool! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which nursing action best helps a patient feel loved and like they belong?

options.A: Providing high-calorie meals for physical recovery
options.B: Encouraging family visits and maintaining social connections
options.C: Strictly restricting all visitors to prevent infections
options.D: Focusing solely on medication administration schedules

explanation: Having loved ones around comforts patients and boosts their emotional well-being. Nursing is caring for the whole person! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why can staying in the hospital for a long time hurt a patient's emotional health?

options.A: It isolates individuals from their normal support systems
options.B: It eliminates the need for any self-care activities
options.C: It automatically cures all underlying physiological diseases
options.D: It forces patients to eat a strictly standardized diet

explanation: Being away from friends, family, and home routines can feel lonely. Recognizing this helps you be a more empathetic nurse. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h5)

question: What can a nurse do to help boost a recovering patient's self-esteem?

options.A: Limiting visitor interactions to resting hours only
options.B: Performing all daily tasks for the patient completely
options.C: Strictly enforcing hospital routines without input

explanation: Letting patients do what they can for themselves builds their confidence and dignity. You are doing great! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the main goal of reaching 'self-actualization' in human needs?

options.B: Securing basic biological survival through hydration
options.C: Obtaining financial stability and housing security
options.D: Achieving personal growth and fulfilling one's potential

explanation: Self-actualization is about becoming the best version of yourself and achieving your dreams. Keep chasing yours in nursing school! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which factor strongly shapes how a patient views and prioritizes their basic needs?

options.A: The brand of hospital uniform worn
options.B: The exact serial number of the bed
options.C: The time of the morning shift handover

explanation: A person's culture and beliefs guide how they view health, food, and healing. Respecting this makes you a fantastic nurse. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why must nurses avoid treating every patient with the exact same approach?

options.A: Hospital regulations forbid treating any two patients identically
options.B: Medical diagnoses dictate every emotional response uniformly
options.C: Individual factors like age and socioeconomics alter need priorities
options.D: Physiological needs change randomly throughout the day

explanation: Every patient's background and life situation is unique, so their care plan should be too. You're mastering individualized care! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which step of the nursing process involves collecting data about unmet needs?
explanation: Assessment is your first step where you gather all the clues about your patient's health. You're building solid clinical habits! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: What is the purpose of the evaluation phase when caring for a patient?

options.A: To select medical diagnoses independently of doctors
options.B: To determine if set goals were met and adjust care
options.C: To administer emergency medications without a doctor's order
options.D: To write initial admission notes for the medical team

explanation: Evaluation lets you check if your nursing actions worked or if you need to try a different approach. Keep up the fantastic daily practice! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)
